title: 進路セミナーⅡ
subtitle: Career Planning Seminar II
educationalGoal: In this course, students consider their career paths by clarifying their working objectives. To find their paths, students conduct industry and company research, and self-analysis to gain an understanding of the circumstances around themselves. In addition, students will acquire basic business and communication skills useful for job hunting.
advice:
This class is provided for the third-year students and the overview is as follows:
1. Introduction of career planning.
2. Industry and companies research.
3. Special lecture 1 (Personnel management officers from companies).
4. Special lecture 2 (Personnel management officers from companies).
5. Writing  C.V. and E.S.
6. Practice exam for employment (SPI, GAB, CAB).
7. Preparing for a job interview.
8. Summary and practical issues.
books: Required Materials will be announced in the class.
requiredKnowledge: Career Planning Seminars I and II are courses for job hunting, and are designed to help students prepare better for employment. Students are required to take this course regardless of whether they intend to seek employment or proceed to graduate school. In addition, the learning results of this subject may be used as reference materials for job placement in the coming year.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the process of deciding a career path.
Be able to collect and analyze necessary information for job hunting.
Be able to explain the level of aptitude and academic ability required by companies.

achievementLevels.ideal: Student with ideal achievement acquire the 3 target abilities. Also, they can judge the company's performance accurately not only from general articles but also from published IR data. Moreover, they are accustomed to SPI and Web tests, and can answer well in a limited time. In the job interview, they can understand the interviewer’s questions accurately and respond quickly according to the situation.
achievementLevels.standard: Student with standard achievement acquire the 3 target abilities at the level of 75%. Also, they can judge the company's performance from general, economic magazine, or newspaper articles. In addition, they can answer SPI and Web test questions at the level of 75% in a limited time. In the interview, they can understand most of the interviewer’s questions and respond in a limited time.

lessons.content:
Introduction of career planning
Learn the schedule of job hunting and how to
decide the companies to approach for
employment.
lessons.assignments:
Review the schedule of job
hunting and standard
properties of companies.

lessons.content:
Industry and companies research
Learn the properties of industry and
companies.
lessons.assignments:
Investigate companies by
using the on-campus search
system and off-campus job
hunting support sites.

companies.

Summarize the points that
helped to select a company.

lessons.assignments:

lessons.content:
Writing C.V./E.S.

Write C.V. and E.S., and

lessons.content:
Practice exam
Answer SPI, Web test, CAB, GAB, etc., in a

lessons.assignments:
Answer more problems using
reference books.

lessons.content:
Job interview
Consider the response to the three major
questions (self-promotion, motivation, and
what you worked hard on at university) in the
interview, and practice speaking.

Summary and practical issues
Learn about things to care about in actual job
hunting.
lessons.assignments:
Summarize what you say at the
interview in a report.

Start job hunting and receive
advice from career advisers
and career development staff
for improving yourself.

              In this course, students consider their career paths by clarifying their working objectives. To find their paths, students conduct industry and company research, and self-analysis to gain an understanding of the circumstances around themselves. In addition, students will acquire basic business and communication skills useful for job hunting.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This class is provided for the third-year students and the overview is as follows:
1. Introduction of career planning.
2. Industry and companies research.
3. Special lecture 1 (Personnel management officers from companies).
4. Special lecture 2 (Personnel management officers from companies).
5. Writing  C.V. and E.S.
6. Practice exam for employment (SPI, GAB, CAB).
7. Preparing for a job interview.
8. Summary and practical issues.

              教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

              Career Planning Seminars I and II are courses for job hunting, and are designed to help students prepare better for employment. Students are required to take this course regardless of whether they intend to seek employment or proceed to graduate school. In addition, the learning results of this subject may be used as reference materials for job placement in the coming year.
